A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Transformer-NFN and the Small Transformer Zoo. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy-prediction experiments on MNIST-Transformers and AGNews-Transformers, including baseline comparisons and component and architecture ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds experiments on symmetry-augmented AGNews-Transformers in Appendix H.4.

M1.justification: The group action, equivariant and invariant polynomial layers, predictor architecture, and implementation pseudocode are retained. The new augmentation experiment evaluates the existing method without introducing a method component.

E1.justification: The MNIST and AGNews datasets and accuracy-prediction tasks remain unchanged. Appendix H.4 adds a distinct input scenario consisting of symmetry-transformed AGNews model weights.

E2.justification: MLP, STATNN, XGBoost, LightGBM, and Random Forest remain the five comparators in Tables 1–2. The new augmentation experiment uses this same comparator set.

E3.justification: Appendix H.4 introduces twofold augmentation of both training and test sets, retaining original weights and adding permutation/scaling transformations. Entries of M and N are sampled uniformly over three ranges: [-1,1], [-10,10], and [-100,100]. Existing experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: The new Appendix H.4 tests robustness of accuracy prediction to symmetry-preserving weight transformations at three scales. Existing component ablations, hidden-dimension/layer studies, and accuracy-threshold analyses are preserved.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-run results with standard errors. New Table 7 follows the existing reporting practice; no increased run count or new uncertainty-estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Original benchmark and ablation values are unchanged. New Table 7 reports Transformer-NFN correlations of 0.912, 0.912, and 0.913 under the three augmentation conditions, with best-baseline gaps of 0.082, 0.079, and 0.080. Its original-condition column repeats existing results.

T1.justification: Assumption (b) in Theorems 3.2 and A.7 changes from full-rank query/key factors to full-rank query-key and value-output products. These products are D-by-D, so the new condition excludes Dk<D or Dv<D, substantially narrowing the central theorem as written. v2 also adds an X factor in Corollary A.5's proof and asymptotic layer-complexity formulas in Appendix F.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same headline claims: maximal attention symmetry, an equivariant Transformer-NFN, and a dataset exceeding 125,000 checkpoints. The claimed superiority over baselines also remains unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix H.4 newly attributes robustness under augmentation to Transformer-NFN's equivariance and baseline deterioration to their lack of symmetry. Appendix F adds an interpretation of computational practicality. The existing qualification that GU omits some transformer-block symmetries remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit public-code repository link in the abstract; v1 directs readers to supplementary source code. Appendix F adds discussion of optimized tensor contractions and GPU parallelization. Existing hyperparameters and implementation pseudocode are retained.

R1.justification: v2 expands background citations and adds Vo et al. (2024), Equivariant Polynomial Functional Networks, to the discussion of parameter-sharing approaches. The central research positioning remains unchanged; publication updates and consolidated duplicate references do not constitute new related work.

P1.justification: The abstract and several results paragraphs are tightened, author/contact information and acknowledgments are updated, and repeated appendix-reference wording is cleaned up. The main section sequence and most explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The document is reformatted throughout into the ICLR template, changing typography, margins, spacing, headers, and figure/table sizing and placement. Table 7 is added, while the existing histograms, scatterplots, and tables retain their content.

improvement.justification: Table 7 adds useful robustness evidence, and the explicit code link improves access information. However, the revised full-rank product requirement substantially restricts the central theorem, while Remark 2 still describes its assumptions as generically satisfied for Dk,Dv≤D. The added validation and this unresolved mismatch between theoretical scope and claimed applicability prevent a confident net-quality judgment.
